acceptance_criteria: BTC window/non-window mean |log return| ratio at least 1.15
spec.alternative_hypothesis: Mean daily absolute log return is higher on expiry-window days than on non-window days (positive window coefficient), with a window/non-window mean ratio of at least 1.15 for BTC.
spec.benchmark: Non-window mean daily absolute log return: the window effect is the window mean minus the non-window mean
cost_assumptions: OKX VIP0 taker fee 0.05% per side, from the OKX public fee schedule (okx.com/fees), checked 2026-11-18; treated as an assumption, not verified for the user's account
Funding rate costs ignored; perpetual funding can exceed taker fees over holding periods
Slippage and market impact ignored; both would reduce any edge
spec.cost_model: No cost gate: H0006 is a volatility-level comparison, not a forecast; there is no trading rule to cost
exclusions: Unconfirmed (forming) OKX bars are excluded; only confirm=1 candles enter the panel
The first daily return row has no lag-1 predictor and is excluded
Bars after the preregistered window end 2026-11-18T16:00Z are out of sample
known_confounders: Absolute returns are strongly autocorrelated (volatility clustering); HAC standard errors (max lag 10) and a block-bootstrap interval account for dependence
The expiry window is only a proxy for dealer-hedging intensity; no dealer position or gamma exposure is measured
Monthly expiries are scarce (about 12 per year); the daily window sample is roughly 280 rows of about 2,100
The T-day daily return spans the Friday 08:00 UTC settlement (bars open 16:00 UTC); the T-1 bar's interval contains the settlement moment and the T bar is the first full post-settlement bar
spec.mechanism: Option expiry concentrates position management (dealer hedging, position closing and repositioning around settlement) in the days before expiry, which may raise realized volatility on window days. The expiry window is only a proxy for dealer-hedging intensity, not a measurement of it. Deribit public data reports whole-market per-contract open interest and Greeks, not dealer positions, so dealer net gamma, dealer positions and hedging flow cannot be verified from public data. This study tests the expiry-window effect itself; any hedging interpretation is inference, not observation. In crypto, forced buying and selling are dominated by perpetual liquidations, open interest and funding rates, and options gamma is only an environment variable.
spec.missing_data_policy: No forward filling; drop incomplete synchronized rows and report the dropped count
model_definition: Mean comparison by OLS of |log return| on the window indicator with HAC standard errors (max lag 10)
Block-bootstrap confidence interval for the window minus non-window mean difference (block 10, 2000 resamples, seed 42)
The mean comparison uses all daily rows in the sample period (train + validation + holdout); the windows define the sample period, not a train/test split for this hypothesis
Wide-window (T-5..T+1), quarterly-vs-monthly and subperiod splits as descriptive checks (not in the test family)
spec.multiple_testing_family: Expiry-window realized-volatility level (2 tests: BTC mean |log return| comparison, ETH mean |log return| comparison)
spec.null_hypothesis: Mean daily absolute log return is the same on expiry-window and non-window days; the window coefficient is zero.
spec.primary_metric: Ratio of mean daily |log return| on expiry-window days to mean daily |log return| on non-window days (BTC primary)
rejection_criteria: Holm-adjusted BTC mean-comparison p-value at or above 0.05
BTC window/non-window mean |log return| ratio below 1.15
spec.research_question: Is mean daily absolute log return (|log return|, a robust realized-volatility proxy) higher on Deribit monthly option expiry-window days (bar-open dates T-3..T) than on non-window days, for BTC (primary) and ETH (secondary) perpetuals?
spec.target_definition: Daily absolute close-to-close log return (|log return|) of the BTC-USDT perpetual (primary) and ETH-USDT perpetual (secondary)
spec.title: Expiry windows raise realized volatility
